subject.title: fix(publish): defer close-proof retries to proof lane

question: Is the persistent Worker/Crabbox proof sufficient to merge this production publication fix with a monitored hosted rollout, despite the default-main workflow boundary preventing a pre-merge end-to-end GitHub Actions canary?
rationale: The patch and isolated runtime contract are well proven, but only a maintainer can accept the residual operational risk of first exercising GitHub App identity and cross-workflow timing after landing.

options.title: Merge with monitored rollout
options.body: Land the fix and immediately verify the first deferred publisher completion reaches apply-proof without a direct close, retry amplification, or new dead letter.

options.title: Require a hosted canary first
options.body: Pause landing until a maintainer-owned disposable repository and GitHub App setup reproduces the repository-dispatch and status-comment handoff.

recommendation.title: Merge with monitored rollout
recommendation.body: Land the fix and immediately verify the first deferred publisher completion reaches apply-proof without a direct close, retry amplification, or new dead letter.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged structured-completion and publication-governance work is the closest current-main ownership signal for deciding the rollout of this new completion kind.
